label: STOPP H6
title: Long-term NSAID or colchicine for gout without allopurinol or febuxostat
statement: Long-term NSAID or colchicine (>3 months) for chronic treatment of gout where there is no contraindication to a xanthine-oxidase inhibitor (e.g., allopurinol, febuxostat) (xanthine-oxidase inhibitors are first choice prophylactic drugs in gout).

plain_summary: For long-term gout prevention, allopurinol or a similar medicine is the first choice, not an anti-inflammatory pain medicine (NSAID) or colchicine.

medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, suppositories and injections count. Skin gels, creams and eye drops do not count, for example Voltaren Emulgel. Aspirin is not in this group. Nurofen Plus and Panafen Plus are ibuprofen with codeine. Nuromol and Maxigesic are ibuprofen with paracetamol. Arthrotec is diclofenac with misoprostol. Vimovo is naproxen with esomeprazole. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

needs_facts.meets: Record the medicine, dose taken and dates of use. Use these to assess any remaining uncovered gout treatment against the same duration and supply-gap limits. If dose or dates remain unclear and would decide the finding, it is still only possible.

rule_for_models: Apply only to people aged 65 years or older. If age is unknown and the other criteria are met, report age as missing and leave the finding unconfirmed. Suspect a finding when a Group A or Group B medicine (a systemic NSAID or colchicine) is supplied for more than 3 months (the first and last supply dates are more than 90 days apart, with no gap of more than 60 days between supplies), the record holds a gout line, and the prolonged gout treatment period being assessed has no overlapping Group C treatment and at least one inhibitor has been assessed as suitable. Cite the supply lines and the gout line. If gout is ruled out or the course is documented solely for another condition, give no finding. If the diagnosis or the reason for the course is missing and the course otherwise qualifies, report only a possible finding and name the missing information. Ask what this NSAID or colchicine course treated only if its purpose is unclear. Use documented treatment dates when available. Otherwise estimate Group C coverage from each supply date and its quantity divided by the prescribed units per day. Count only dispensed quantities and combine covered dates without counting the same day twice. If coverage remains uncertain and would decide the finding, report only a possible finding and ask which inhibitor was taken, its dose and the actual dates of use. An unknown answer leaves cover uncertain. If Group C covers the entire assessed period, give no finding. Assess any uncovered course against the same duration and supply-gap rules. If both inhibitors are contraindicated, there is no finding. If suitability is unknown, report a possible finding and name the missing information. Cite the assessment of suitability when confirming a finding. If the course otherwise qualifies but unclear or as-needed directions leave regular use uncertain, report only a possible finding. Ask whether the person took it regularly for gout during this course or only in short courses. Short courses alone give no finding. Unknown use leaves the finding possible.
cannot_be_seen: Why the NSAID or colchicine was started, because colchicine is also used for other conditions. Also whether allopurinol was tried before the record began, any reaction to it, kidney function, and medicines supplied by another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether a xanthine-oxidase inhibitor such as allopurinol is suitable for long-term gout prevention in place of the current medicine.
